exams.syllabus: ABRSM Harp Practical Grades from 2025. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: Marks
Pieces 3 x 30 = 90; Scales and arpeggios 21; Sight-reading 21; Aural tests 18; total 150. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119. A pass in each component is not required.
Choosing pieces

One piece from each of Lists A (faster, agile), B (lyrical, expressive), C (varied traditions and styles). Same lists as Performance Grades. Listed arrangements must use stated edition; chords may be spread or notes omitted for small hands. Memory optional. Separate pedal harp and non-pedal (lever) harp syllabuses, Grades 1-8; no Initial Grade. Pedal harp from Grade 4 generally needs 46+ strings; lever harp from Grade 3 needs 34+ strings (bottom C two octaves below middle C or lower). Candidate brings and tunes own harp and is given time for pedal/lever changes. 2019 pieces allowed until 31 Dec 2025. Syllabus valid from 1 June 2025.
Digital exams
Same repertoire lists are used for ABRSM Performance Grades; marks cannot be transferred between Practical Grades and Performance Grades. This Practical Grades exam is face-to-face.
sections: Scales & technical work

All from memory, legato, even notes; any starting octave if range covered; arpeggios/dominant sevenths root position unless stated. PEDAL: C, F majors and A minor (natural or harmonic) 1 oct, hands separately. Scale in thirds: C major 1 oct hands separately. Arpeggios C, F majors, A minor 1 oct, hands separately or divided between the hands (candidate's choice). NON-PEDAL: identical requirements (C, F, A minor; thirds in C; same arpeggios).
Sight-reading

Half a minute to prepare, unaccompanied. Up to 6 bars, 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, C major; each hand separately, single notes; h. h q values; f and p. (Same parameters for pedal and non-pedal; accidentals via pedal or lever changes.)
Aural & other tests
Grade 1 aural: (A) clap pulse, say 2 or 3 time; (B) sing 3 two-bar echoes (major, tonic-mediant); (C) spot a pitch change (near beginning/end); (D) questions on dynamics and articulation.

sections: Scales & technical work

sections: Scales & technical work

sections: Scales & technical work

All from memory, legato, even notes; any starting octave if range covered; arpeggios/dominant sevenths root position unless stated. PEDAL: scales E, Gb, Ab majors and C#, Eb, F minors (harmonic and melodic) 4 oct, hands separately or together an octave or tenth apart. Contrary motion scale Ab major 2 oct hands together starting an octave apart. Etouffe scale in octaves F harmonic minor 1 oct LH. Scale in harmonics Gb major 1 oct hands separately. Arpeggios same keys 4 oct (root, first or second inversion; hands separately, together or divided). Dominant sevenths in Ab and Gb, 4 oct, second inversion; plus narrow-position version divided between hands (root position). Diminished seventh from C#, 4 oct. NON-PEDAL: C# natural minor 3 oct; Eb, E, G majors, C, E harmonic minors 2 oct (octave or tenth apart); C, E melodic minors RH 2 oct; Dorian on E 2 oct hands together; etouffe scale in octaves C harmonic minor 1 oct LH; harmonics Eb major 1 oct. Sight-reading

Half a minute to prepare, unaccompanied. Up to 20 bars; adds 7/8, 7/4, 4-note chords per hand, pedal/lever changes, clef changes, etouffe, hands sharing a stave, harmonics, 8va/8vb, simple ornaments, tempo changes. (Same parameters for pedal and non-pedal; accidentals via pedal or lever changes.)

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Harp Practical Grades from 2025. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: Marks
Pieces 3 x 30 = 90; Scales and arpeggios 21; Sight-reading 21; Aural tests 18; total 150. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119. A pass in each component is not required.
Choosing pieces

One piece from each of Lists A (faster, agile), B (lyrical, expressive), C (varied traditions and styles). Same lists as Performance Grades. Listed arrangements must use stated edition; chords may be spread or notes omitted for small hands. Memory optional. Separate pedal harp and non-pedal (lever) harp syllabuses, Grades 1-8; no Initial Grade. Pedal harp from Grade 4 generally needs 46+ strings; lever harp from Grade 3 needs 34+ strings (bottom C two octaves below middle C or lower). Candidate brings and tunes own harp and is given time for pedal/lever changes. 2019 pieces allowed until 31 Dec 2025. Syllabus valid from 1 June 2025.
Before you enter
Grade 5 or above in ABRSM Music Theory, Practical Musicianship, or a Practical Grades solo Jazz instrument is required before Grades 6, 7 or 8.
Digital exams
Same repertoire lists are used for ABRSM Performance Grades; marks cannot be transferred between Practical Grades and Performance Grades. This Practical Grades exam is face-to-face.
sections: Scales & technical work

All from memory, legato, even notes; any starting octave if range covered; arpeggios/dominant sevenths root position unless stated. PEDAL: scales Cb, Eb, F# majors and Ab, C, Eb minors (harmonic and melodic) 4 oct, hands separately or together a sixth or tenth apart. Contrary motion scale Eb harmonic minor 2 oct starting a sixth apart. Scale in octaves a sixth apart with etouffe in LH: Eb major 1 oct. Harmonics scale Ab harmonic minor 1 oct hands together. Arpeggios same keys 4 oct (root, first or second inversion). Dominant sevenths in Cb and F#, 4 oct, any inversion incl. third; diminished seventh from F#, 4 oct, plus narrow position (root position). NON-PEDAL: F major 3 oct; C, A majors, F# natural minor, A and D harmonic minors 2 oct (sixth or tenth apart); A, D melodic minors RH 2 oct; major blues on F and minor blues on D 3 oct RH; harmonics F major 1 oct hands together; staccato chromatic scale from D 1 oct RH. Arpeggios F major 3 oct/4 oct divided; C, A majors, A, D, F# minors 2 oct/3 oct divided; dominant sevenths in F and A (3 oct/4 oct divided, all inversions); diminished seventh from F# (3 oct, 4 oct divided, narrow position 3 oct).
Sight-reading

Half a minute to prepare, unaccompanied. Up to 32 bars; adds 12/8, very short note values, pres de la table, time-signature changes. (Same parameters for pedal and non-pedal; accidentals via pedal or lever changes.)
Aural & other tests

(A) sing/play lowest part of three-part phrase, identify cadence (incl. plagal) and its three chords with positions; (B) sing lower part of two-part phrase from score; (C) identify modulations in two passages; (D) describe characteristic features of a piece.

exams.syllabus: Trinity Strings syllabus (harp, from 2025). Lists read from the board's official repertoire pages.
comps: Marks

Face-to-face (all instruments): 3 pieces x 22 = 66 (each piece: fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8); technical work 14; supporting tests 20 (2 x 10). Total 100. Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No section has to be passed individually. Per-piece bands: 19-22 Distinction, 16-18 Merit, 13-15 Pass.
Exam length

Face-to-face bowed strings: Initial 11 min; G1-3 13 min; G4-5 18 min; G6-7 23 min; G8 28 min. Harp: Initial 13 min; G1-3 15 min; G4-5 20 min; G6-7 25 min; G8 30 min. Section order is the candidate's choice (default: bowed strings pieces first; harp technical work first). Digital: no exam length stated.
Choosing pieces

Pieces come from the separate repertoire list (trinitycollege.com/strings). Initial-Grade 3: any 3 pieces (4 on digital Repertoire-only), max one duet (bowed strings only; upper part, partner live or pre-recorded on a bowed string instrument, never piano), max one unaccompanied piece. Grades 4-5: any 3, max one unaccompanied. Grades 6-8: list split into Group A and Group B; choose 3 with at least one from each group; max one unaccompanied. Own composition may replace one listed piece at every grade (duration Initial 30-40s rising to 3-4 min at G7-8; any notation to G5, staff notation required G6-8; copy given to examiner/uploaded). Violin: a piece/set from the Scottish traditional fiddle list at the same grade may replace one piece (max one unaccompanied or fiddle item); G6-8 one piece may be played on viola from the Viola list (technical work and supporting tests on violin). Viola: G6-8 one piece may be on violin from the Violin list. Double bass: max one all-pizzicato piece. Harp: Initial-G3 pieces playable on pedal or lever harp unless marked. Pieces published with accompaniment must be accompanied (single instrument, piano unless approved). Face-to-face: recorded accompaniment/backing track allowed up to Grade 3, live accompaniment from Grade 4; page turner allowed G6-8. Vibrato expected from Grade 5 (bowed). Repeats of 4 bars or fewer observed, longer repeats omitted unless stated; D.C./D.S. observed; cadenzas only if stated; memory optional (no extra marks). Teachers may help tune up to G5; G6-8 candidates tune unaided.
Digital exams

Two pathways, same entry process; exam filmed as one continuous take. Technical work pathway: 3 pieces x 22 = 66, technical work 14, overall performance criteria 20 = 100. Technical work played as one unit in listed order (before, after or between pieces); bowed strings play the bowing exercise (not at Initial) then EITHER one fixed set of scales/arpeggios/technical exercises (set A or set B - every item in the set is played, with bowings specified, from memory) OR two studies (G1-5) / two orchestral extracts from different groups (G6-8), candidate's choice; harp plays the listed scales/arpeggios/exercises OR two studies OR (pedal harp G6-8) two orchestral extracts. Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x 25 = 100, no technical work or supporting tests. Same grade boundaries as face-to-face. Backing tracks/recorded accompaniment allowed at all grades in digital exams.
sections: Technical work

No bowing exercise; EITHER 1) scales & arpeggios from memory (min crotchet = 60, one note per quaver, mf): C major and A minor (harmonic or natural) scales 1 oct divided between hands; C major and A minor arpeggios to the 5th, hands separately; plus exercises, prepare all three, play two (candidate one, examiner one; music allowed): Swinging (arpeggio patterns), Small Scissors (thirds), Big Scissors (sixths). OR 2) studies, prepare all three, play two (candidate one, examiner one; music allowed): Bears in a Cage, Fanfare, Rodeo.
Supporting tests

Choose 2 of: sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge. Sight reading (30s prep, at a lower level than the exam; cumulative): 2 and 4 time signatures; crotchets and minims; moderato, mf; hands separately, range of a 5th; keys C major. Aural: 4-bar major melody in 2 time - clap pulse stressing strong beat (3rd hearing); dynamic f or p; legato or staccato; highest or lowest of first three notes. Improvisation: stylistic - 4 bars over piano (march or lullaby, 4 time, C major, chords I and V); motivic - 4-6-bar unaccompanied response to a 2-bar motif; harmonic - unaccompanied over a chord sequence (4 bars once; I-V; keys C major). Musical knowledge (questions on own pieces): pitch names, note durations, clefs/staves/barlines, identify key/time signatures, basic terms and signs.

comps: Marks

Face-to-face (all instruments): 3 pieces x 22 = 66 (each piece: fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8); technical work 14; supporting tests 20 (2 x 10). Total 100. Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No section has to be passed individually. Per-piece bands: 19-22 Distinction, 16-18 Merit, 13-15 Pass.
Exam length

Face-to-face bowed strings: Initial 11 min; G1-3 13 min; G4-5 18 min; G6-7 23 min; G8 28 min. Harp: Initial 13 min; G1-3 15 min; G4-5 20 min; G6-7 25 min; G8 30 min. Section order is the candidate's choice (default: bowed strings pieces first; harp technical work first). Digital: no exam length stated.
Choosing pieces

Pieces come from the separate repertoire list (trinitycollege.com/strings). Initial-Grade 3: any 3 pieces (4 on digital Repertoire-only), max one duet (bowed strings only; upper part, partner live or pre-recorded on a bowed string instrument, never piano), max one unaccompanied piece. Grades 4-5: any 3, max one unaccompanied. Grades 6-8: list split into Group A and Group B; choose 3 with at least one from each group; max one unaccompanied. Own composition may replace one listed piece at every grade (duration Initial 30-40s rising to 3-4 min at G7-8; any notation to G5, staff notation required G6-8; copy given to examiner/uploaded). Violin: a piece/set from the Scottish traditional fiddle list at the same grade may replace one piece (max one unaccompanied or fiddle item); G6-8 one piece may be played on viola from the Viola list (technical work and supporting tests on violin). Viola: G6-8 one piece may be on violin from the Violin list. Double bass: max one all-pizzicato piece. Harp: Initial-G3 pieces playable on pedal or lever harp unless marked. Pieces published with accompaniment must be accompanied (single instrument, piano unless approved). Face-to-face: recorded accompaniment/backing track allowed up to Grade 3, live accompaniment from Grade 4; page turner allowed G6-8. Vibrato expected from Grade 5 (bowed). Repeats of 4 bars or fewer observed, longer repeats omitted unless stated; D.C./D.S. observed; cadenzas only if stated; memory optional (no extra marks). Teachers may help tune up to G5; G6-8 candidates tune unaided.
Digital exams

Two pathways, same entry process; exam filmed as one continuous take. Technical work pathway: 3 pieces x 22 = 66, technical work 14, overall performance criteria 20 = 100. Technical work played as one unit in listed order (before, after or between pieces); bowed strings play the bowing exercise (not at Initial) then EITHER one fixed set of scales/arpeggios/technical exercises (set A or set B - every item in the set is played, with bowings specified, from memory) OR two studies (G1-5) / two orchestral extracts from different groups (G6-8), candidate's choice; harp plays the listed scales/arpeggios/exercises OR two studies OR (pedal harp G6-8) two orchestral extracts. Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x 25 = 100, no technical work or supporting tests. Same grade boundaries as face-to-face. sections: Technical work

Pedal harp: EITHER 1) Ab, E major and C#, F# minor (harmonic and melodic) scales and arpeggios, plus Ab major contrary motion; 2 oct hands together (crotchet = 90, f or p). Lever harp: E or Ab major (per tuning, state on form), G and D minor (harmonic and melodic, melodic RH only), contrary motion on E or Ab; arpeggios E or Ab major, G, D minor. Both: exercises A Bit Jazzy, Rocking Chair, PDLT. OR 2) studies: Shining Scales, Cool Dude, Elizabeth's Revel. (Prepare three, play two.)
Supporting tests

Choose 2 of: sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge. Sight reading (30s prep, about two grades below the exam; cumulative): adds dotted crotchets, quaver rests; cresc./decresc.; more pedal changes (pedal harp); keys D, A major; E, D minor (pedal). comps: Marks

Face-to-face (all instruments): 3 pieces x 22 = 66 (each piece: fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8); technical work 14; supporting tests 20 (2 x 10). Total 100. Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No section has to be passed individually. Per-piece bands: 19-22 Distinction, 16-18 Merit, 13-15 Pass.
Exam length

Face-to-face bowed strings: Initial 11 min; G1-3 13 min; G4-5 18 min; G6-7 23 min; G8 28 min. Harp: Initial 13 min; G1-3 15 min; G4-5 20 min; G6-7 25 min; G8 30 min. Section order is the candidate's choice (default: bowed strings pieces first; harp technical work first). Digital: no exam length stated.
Choosing pieces

Pieces come from the separate repertoire list (trinitycollege.com/strings). Initial-Grade 3: any 3 pieces (4 on digital Repertoire-only), max one duet (bowed strings only; upper part, partner live or pre-recorded on a bowed string instrument, never piano), max one unaccompanied piece. Grades 4-5: any 3, max one unaccompanied. Grades 6-8: list split into Group A and Group B; choose 3 with at least one from each group; max one unaccompanied. Own composition may replace one listed piece at every grade (duration Initial 30-40s rising to 3-4 min at G7-8; any notation to G5, staff notation required G6-8; copy given to examiner/uploaded). Violin: a piece/set from the Scottish traditional fiddle list at the same grade may replace one piece (max one unaccompanied or fiddle item); G6-8 one piece may be played on viola from the Viola list (technical work and supporting tests on violin). exams.name: ARSM
exams.full: Associate of the Royal Schools of Music — ABRSM Level 4 Diploma in Music Performance
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 5), about the end of the first year of an undergraduate course; 90 credits, 54 GLH, 900 TQT
comps: Entry requirement

A pass at Grade 8 on the same or a closely related instrument: ABRSM Practical or Performance Grade 8, or an accepted equivalent from another board (for example Trinity, LCM, MTB, Guildhall, RIAM, AMEB or UNISA). No theory prerequisite.
Format & marks

Face-to-face (public venue or private visit) OR digital (video recorded at a time and place of the candidate's choice, with no fixed sessions; video uploaded at booking or within 28 days). Performance only: 30-minute programme (±2 min), timed from the first note to the last. Marks: pieces 30 (60%) + performance as a whole 20 (40%) = 50. Distinction 45–50, Merit 40–44, Pass 34–39, Below Pass 17–33.
Programme rules

At least 20 minutes from the ARSM repertoire list for the instrument, plus up to 10 minutes of own-choice music at Grade 8 standard or above. No written or spoken elements and no other tests (no viva, no programme notes, no quick study). Candidates submit a programme form, or enter programme details online for digital exams.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ARSM repertoire list for harp, read from the ABRSM PDF (56 entries). All works are for pedal harp unless otherwise indicated; candidates may present one work on non-pedal harp as the related-instrument option. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

Pathway as of Oct 2026: ARSM (L4) → LRSM (L6) → FRSM (L7). DipABRSM is withdrawn (last date 31 Dec 2023). The old-format LRSM closed 30 Apr 2024 and the old FRSM closed 31 Oct 2024. All three current diplomas require only Grade 8 in the instrument (ABRSM or an equivalent board for LRSM/FRSM). No Grade 5 or 6 theory prerequisite is stated for any current performance diploma. Under the old syllabus, Grade 5 theory appeared only as a condition on some substitutions. ARSM has no written element. LRSM/FRSM need a written (2,000 / 3,500 words) or spoken-video (10 / 17 min) supporting-evidence submission. Digital exams have no fixed sessions: book, pay and upload any time; for digital ARSM the video goes in at booking or within 28 days. Specific LRSM/FRSM upload windows weren't stated in the spec, which refers to abrsm.org/how-to-book. ABRSM discontinued printed diploma syllabuses, and lists are updated online, so re-check the abrsm.org pages before entering. abrsm.org HTML pages returned redirect errors to the fetch tool, so some details come from the PDFs and ABRSM's Taiwan mirror.
General rules (all instruments)

Both LRSM and FRSM programmes must be balanced and varied: a variety of moods, keys and tempi and at least two pieces or movements contrasting by period or style. Works and movements must be played complete unless the repertoire list says otherwise, and any list-specific instructions must be followed. Music published with an accompaniment must be performed with one; any suitable instrument may accompany provided the candidate stays the main soloist, candidates arrange their own accompanist, and pre-recorded accompaniments are not allowed unless the composer intended them. Memory is not required (but encouraged if it helps). Any edition matching the list entry may be used and own-choice music must exist as a legible, fully notated score; performing from unauthorised photocopies of copyright editions is not allowed. Own-choice may include the candidate's own composition or arrangement but must still be at or above the required standard, and ABRSM cannot give prior approval of own-choice standard. An audience is encouraged but not required. Infringements (wrong length, too much own choice without approval, wrong movements, edited video) can bring a warning, mark deduction or disqualification. A video can only ever be submitted once, and the same Unit 2 work cannot be reused at a higher level.

comps: Entry requirement
Same as LRSM: Grade 8 (or equivalent, or approved professional experience) in the instrument presented. LRSM is NOT a formal prerequisite under the new spec.
Format & marks

Digital only. Continuous-take video recital of 55 min ±10%. Woodwind may take one break of up to 5 min. Marks and bands are the same as LRSM: 30/30/15 = 75; Distinction 68–75, Merit 60–67, Pass 50–59.
Programme rules

At least 50% from the FRSM list; own choice up to 50% (about 27 min) at or beyond LRSM standard. Unit 2 supporting evidence (same four options; analysis option covers a 30-min section): 3,500 words ±10% written OR a 17-min ±10% spoken video. No viva voce and no quick study.

Unit 2 is a written submission (3500 words, plus or minus 10%, PDF) or a spoken video presentation (17 minutes, plus or minus 10%) on one of four options: Informing your audience, Detailed analysis, Programming your performance, or Preparation for performance, based on substantial personal research and reflection. exams.name: ATCL
exams.full: Associate of Trinity College London (Music Performance)
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 4/5); Ofqual qualification no. 600/0949/4
comps: Entry requirement
None formal: no minimum age, no prior grade or theory qualification required.
Format & marks

Available face-to-face (at Trinity centres, no audience) and digital (one continuous unedited video, max 3GB, uploaded with written programme, any approval letter and one scan per piece; audience allowed). Same structure, criteria and certificate in both formats. Recital 32-38 min performing time (exam slot 40 min). Marked out of 100: Recital 96 (Fluency & accuracy 32, Technical assurance & application 32, Musical sense & communication 32) + Programme & planning 4 (written programme 2, planning/balance/construction 2). Results: Distinction 80-100, Pass 60-79, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No Merit band.
Programme rules

Programme of at least two works (singing/percussion three), showing a range of moods, styles and tempi; any order. Works complete unless the list specifies movements. Programme may be all list repertoire, list + own-choice, or all own-choice; any own-choice (or single movements of works listed as complete) must be pre-approved as a whole programme via trinitycollege.com/approvals. Accompanied candidates may include unaccompanied works up to 40% of the programme. No viva/discussion component is mentioned in the March 2026 syllabus. Written programme (composers, titles, timings) required; no full programme notes at ATCL. Trinity describes ATCL as equivalent to a first-year undergraduate recital.
sections: About the repertoire list

Programmes may use list pieces, a mix of list and own-choice pieces, or only own-choice pieces; any programme with own-choice repertoire must be pre-approved and own-choice pieces must be of comparable demand. Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
